headline: World's Largest Wildlife Crossing Opens on California Highway
meta_description: California's Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing, the world's largest, opens this December across Highway 101 with 6,000 native plants.
summary_short: California's groundbreaking wildlife crossing will help animals safely traverse 10 lanes of Highway 101 when it opens this December.
body:
California is preparing to open the world's largest wildlife crossing this December, creating a safe passage for animals across 10 lanes of Highway 101. The Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing represents a major step forward in protecting local wildlife from vehicle collisions while allowing natural migration patterns to continue.

The crossing has been planted with 6,000 native plants, designed to create a natural habitat bridge that encourages animals to use the passage safely. This ambitious infrastructure project reflects growing recognition that major highways can fragment ecosystems and endanger wildlife populations. By providing a dedicated crossing point, the structure aims to reduce animal-vehicle collisions while maintaining ecological connectivity across one of California's busiest transportation corridors.
quick_facts: World's largest wildlife crossing opens in California this December
Features 6,000 native plants creating natural habitat
